title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling Playbook, Benchmarks, Release Notes & Runbooks (2027-06-01)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This consolidated reference captures the serving runtime architecture, kernel scheduling model, profiling playbook, benchmarking suite, recent releases, known issues, and operational runbooks for Redwood Inference\u000E2\u000E2s serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, performance SREs, release managers, and platform owners.

Scope:
- Architecture overview and call flows for model inference paths (stateless request, warm KV-cache, long-lived chat sessions).
- Kernel and scheduling strategies for GPU pools (Batched, Streaming, MPS-like multiplexing).
- Profiling and instrumentation playbook: what to collect, how to triage, and common remediations.
- Benchmarking suite: workloads, metrics, and CI gating.
- Recent release notes (v4.2.x) with compatibility and rollback guidance.
- Known issues and mitigations.
- Runbooks and on-call procedures for performance incidents.

1) Architecture overview

Short intro: The serving runtime is a high-throughput, low-latency inference engine optimized for transformer-based LLMs. The runtime supports three primary request classes: short (<=64 tokens), medium conversational (<=512 tokens with KV reuse), and long-running generations (>2k tokens).

Key components (logical):
- Router: request classification, policy-based routing (latency/cost/region), and fallback to model variants.
- Frontend workers: admission control, tokenization, request shaping, and prefix caching lookup.
- Scheduler: determines kernel launches, batching windows, and GPU assignment.
- Execution engine: model kernels (FP32/FP16/INT8 with quantization profiles), KV cache manager, and attention optimizations.
- Metrics/Tracing: high-cardinality fixed tags per token and per-request traces to Zipkin/Tempo and Prometheus.

SLOs and targets:
- P99 latency per token (short requests) <= 80ms
- P50 latency (short requests) <= 12ms
- End-to-end 95th percentile for conversational requests <= 250ms for <= 512 tokens workloads
- Throughput: target aggregate token/sec per GPU reported in fleet dashboards (see Benchmarking section)

Ownership and escalation: runtime-core owns core scheduler and kernels; infra-fleet owns GPU provisioning and drivers. On-call escalation: runtime oncall -> infra-fleet -> hardware vendor (if suspected).

2) Kernel scheduling model

Design goals: maximize GPU utilization while preserving latency SLOs for latency-sensitive classes. The scheduler implements a hybrid policy that combines:
- Continuous batching (micro-batches with max_wait_ms and adaptive size)
- Priority preemption for latency-tiered requests (real-time lanes)
- KV-aware co-scheduling for conversational flows to keep KV cache hot on the assigned GPU

Scheduler parameters (defaults):
- max_batch_tokens = 32768
- max_batch_time_ms = 8
- priority_real_time_fraction = 0.15
- kv_hot_window_ms = 30000

Practical notes:
- Use the real-time lane for interactive UI flows. The lane reduces batching delay (max_batch_time_ms=1-3ms) at cost of throughput.
- For throughput-oriented offline jobs, increase max_batch_time_ms to 12-20ms and raise max_batch_tokens.
- Preemption strategy is cooperative: long-running kernel launches include a cooperative checkpoint to allow high-priority kernels to be scheduled between micro-iterations.

3) Profiling & instrumentation playbook

When to profile: any increase in P95/P99 latency, regression after a kernel or scheduler change, or new model onboarding.

Data to collect (minimum):
- Per-request trace (sampling 1:1000 for normal, 1:50 during investigation).
- GPU metrics: GPU utilization (%), SM occupancy, memory bandwidth, GPU memory used, pci-e stalls (via nvtop / nvidia-smi dmon / telegraf).
- Kernel timeline: per-kernel launch time, queue wait time, kernel duration (ns).
- Scheduler logs: batch composition, batch wait time distribution, preempt events.
- KV cache hit ratio by session id and age.

Commands and tools:
- Local reproducer: ./tools/run_repro.sh --model gpt-3-like --tokens 512 --concurrency 8
- Kernel tracing: Nsight Systems: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o /tmp/profile.nsys \\
- GPU counters: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o TD
- Micro-kernel timeline: PERF_COLLECTOR (internal) --session $SESSION_ID --output /tmp/trace.json

Triage checklist (ordered):
1. Confirm regression with benchmarks (CI synthetic and sampled production).
2. Collect a request-level trace and GPU timeline for the window.
3. Check for recent deploys (kernel, scheduler, driver).
4. Inspect KV cache hit ratio and session placement churn.
5. If kernel-duration dominated, isolate model/kernel; if queue wait dominated, inspect batching window and preemption config.
6. Apply mitigation (rollback, adjust max_batch_time_ms, add capacity) and validate.

4) Benchmarking suite

Goals: deterministic, reproducible workload profiles for gating PRs and validating capacity planning. Benchmarks live in repo: infra/benchmarks/serving-suite. CI triggers: nightly, pre-release, and manual.

Workload profiles included:
- interactive-short: 8 concurrent users, 32 tokens average, target latency < 20ms P95
- conv-medium: 200 concurrent sessions, 512 token median, target latency < 250ms P95
- long-generation: 16 concurrent, 2k+ tokens, throughput focused (tokens/sec)
- embeddings-batch: CPU/GPU hybrid workload for embedding models

Metrics recorded:
- P50/P95/P99 per-request latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, KV hit ratio, error rate.

CI gating rules (examples):
- Any change to kernels or scheduler must not regress P99 by more than 5% on conv-medium profile.
- New model onboarding requires baseline run on at least 2 GPU families (A100, H100) with documented quantization profile.

Running the suite locally: 
1) Source the ci env: source infra/benchmarks/env.sh
2) Run: make bench-profile PROFILE=conv-medium DEVICE=gpu NUM_NODES=1
3) Results: artifacts/serving-suite/<timestamp>/report.html and metrics.json

5) Release notes (v4.2.0 - 2027-05-20 to 2027-06-01)
- v4.2.0 (2027-05-20): Scheduler improvements: adaptive batching that reduces P95 by ~18% for medium conversational workloads. Default max_batch_time_ms reduced from 12ms -> 8ms.
- v4.2.1 (2027-05-27): Hotfix: corrected KV cache eviction bug causing session churn under burst load.
- v4.2.2 (2027-06-01): Backported kernel micro-optimizations for INT8 matmul; improved stability on H100 drivers.

Upgrade guidance:
- Staged rollout (canary 2% -> 25% -> 100%) using the Console rollout tool. Monitor P95/P99, error rate, and GPU OOM metrics.
- Rollback procedure: use console rollback to previous model/runtime version and run the smoke benchmark immediately. If rollback fails, follow runbook: serving-runtime rollback (section below).

6) Known issues (active)
- #KRNL-214: Under synthetic uniform long sequences (>4096 tokens), preemption may not occur promptly leading to P99 spikes. Mitigation: set priority_real_time_fraction to 0.2 and increase preempt check interval to 4ms.
- #KV-137: Rare KV cache desync after driver update; symptoms: higher cold-start latency and KV hit ratio drop. Temporary mitigation: restart frontend workers and warm sessions, permanent fix in v4.3.0.
- #H100-42: Certain H100 drivers cause sporadic memory fragmentation leading to OOMs for large batched embeddings. Mitigation: pin driver to known-good 535.104.07 and limit max_batch_tokens for embedding jobs.

7) Runbooks (operational playbooks)

Performance incident (P95/P99 latency regression) - Quick steps:
1. Open incident on PagerDuty and tag runtime-performance.
2. Capture time window and run the nightly benchmark for the same window to confirm.
3. Pull one or more request traces and GPU timelines. Attach to the incident.
4. Toggle real-time lane off (Console -> runtime config) to isolate batching effects.
5. If immediate mitigation needed: increase fleet capacity (scale-out) or reduce max_batch_time_ms to 1-3ms for critical slices.
6. If kernel regressions suspected, roll back to previous runtime version and run smoke bench.
7. Post-incident: complete postmortem with root cause, actions, and test coverage for CI.

Rollback runbook (if rollout fails):
1. Trigger rollback from Console to previous runtime version.
2. Run smoke benchmark: make bench-profile PROFILE=interactive-short DEVICE=gpu NUM_NODES=1
3. If rollback does not restore expected metrics, escalate to infra-fleet and collect driver/kernel traces.
4. Notify customers on affected tiers if incident >30 minutes.

8) Onboarding new models (short checklist)
1. Run model through quantization-profiles and select default profile (FP16/INT8).
2. Run full serving-suite on A100 and H100.
3. Validate KV cache behavior for conversational flows.
4. Submit release PR with benchmark artifacts and expected perf delta.

Appendix: Example kernel debugging commands
- nsight: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o /tmp/profile $(pidof serving-runtime)
- gpu counters: NVIDIA-SMI (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv)
- collect logs: journalctl -u serving-runtime -S "2027-06-01 12:00:00" -U "2027-06-01 12:15:00" > /tmp/serving-logs.txt
